title: Crossplane stage synchronizer with credit-based NCCL windowing
creator: Priya Nair
description: Add a crossplane stage synchronizer that enforces a credit-based communication window for NCCL to safely overlap collective transfers with local kernel execution across mixed tensor/pipeline-parallel topologies. Goal is to reduce prefill tail latency and improve steady-state decode throughput for multi-GPU serving without regressing single-GPU latency or determinism.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic ordering preserved across pipeline and tensor stages when synchronizer is enabled
Prefill 99th percentile latency reduced by >=12% on representative Llama-variant 16B workload compared to baseline (no-credit-window), measured across c5/ampere-like cluster
Decode throughput increased by >=8% for batched streaming scenarios without increased token error rates in eval set
Stress test under node preemption and heterogenous bandwidth shows graceful degeneration (automatic shrinking of window) and no deadlocks
Automated unit and integration tests merged; e2e perf benchmark job added to CI with fixed seed reproducibility
tasks: Spec credit-based windowing algorithm and API (synchronizer + per-stage credits)
Prototype runtime hooks for reserving/releasing comm credits in prefill and decode paths
Integrate with NCCL rendezvous layer to support non-blocking enqueues and windowed progress
Add kernel-hint annotations so scheduler can avoid launching heavy kernels when credits are low
Run perf sweep across sequence lengths (32/128/1024) and microbatch sizes, capture traces
Implement fallback policy that shrinks window under congestion and records telemetry
Write integration tests simulating heterogenous NIC speeds and unstable links
Create rollout plan: canary on dedicated cluster, monitor cost/latency dashboards
risks_and_tradeoffs: Tighter coupling between runtime and NCCL progress increases complexity of upgrade paths for on-prem customers
Aggressive windowing can starve the compute pipeline or introduce jitter if not tuned per-topology
Adding credit flow control increases code paths for failure scenarios (need thorough testing)
May interact with existing KV cache prefetch heuristics; risk of regressions in cache hit-rate unless coordinated
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: RFC posted — rationale, algorithm sketch (credit tokens per stage, dynamic shrink/expand), and API surface for runtime. Initial feedback: prefer explicit telemetry fields for credits and backpressure events.
2026-02-25: Micro-prototype implemented in local dev cluster: credit allocator + simple NCCL enqueue wrapper. Observed 9% throughput uplift on small decode tests with 4xA100 topology.

2026-03-03: Experiments expanded to tensor+pipeline mix (2 tensor shards x 2 pipeline stages). Prefill 95/99p latency improved but tail occasionally spiked under cross-traffic — root cause: window growth logic overestimated available NIC bandwidth.
2026-03-06: Decision to add bandwidth-aware scaling: synchronizer samples NIC throughput via perf counters and conservatively caps window growth. Added to spec and prioritized implementation.

2026-03-09: Design review with runtime, infra, and QA. Action items: (1) add deterministic test harness for ordering, (2) add canary job config in console for runtime-1.22, (3) instrument credit drop events in observability dashboard.

2026-03-12: PR #4187 opened with initial implementation of credit accounting and NCCL windowing wrapper (link in attachments). Benchmarks in CI show 11% 99p reduction on 128-seq prefill; further tuning scheduled.
Blocked: Need kernel-hint plumbing from kernel-selection team to prevent compute-heavy kernels when credits low (dependency ENG-27184).
notes_and_decisions: Keep default synchronizer disabled for hosted customers until runtime-1.22 GA; make it opt-in via cluster config for Dedicated/Private during canary
Expose per-route credit policy in Console: conservative, balanced, aggressive. Default = balanced
Use exponential backoff to regrow windows after shrink to avoid oscillation under bursty cross-traffic
Fallback policy: if NCCL enqueues error or timeout, immediately drain outstanding credits and fallback to serialized comm mode for the affected pipeline stage
review_feedback: From: Elena Park (Infra Lead) — recommend adding a lightweight heartbeat to detect stalled outstanding collectives and emit alarms
From: Marcus Lee (QA) — request reproducible CI scenario that injects packet loss and variable bandwidth
From: Hannah Cho (Product) — include rollback thresholds in rollout plan and ensure cost telemetry is recorded per-route
next_steps: Complete kernel-hint integration (coordinate with ENG-27184) and land corresponding PR
Add heterogenous NIC perf tests to CI and run overnight sweep
Create canary config and telemetry dashboard panels for credit usage and backpressure events
Prepare runbook for on-call describing failure modes and mitigation (shrink/disable synchronizer)
